revision_history.change_rationale: Refined connection routing, official resources and semantic micro-motion after prior visual rejection.
Added semantic legend and synchronized Engineering labels to routed SVG paths.
Network engineering review required a connection-centric topology that makes spine, leaf, access, security, OOB and evidenced link semantics more directly readable to engineers.

iteration_4_engineering_changes: T02 Engineering mode now uses a generic role-driven connection-centric lane layout for AUTO-layout packages: Security/Services, Edge/Border/Interconnect, Spine/Fabric Core, Leaf/Access, Workload/Storage/Services and Management/OOB.
NORMALIZED_HINTS layouts are deliberately preserved; the shared engineering layer does not overwrite project-authored explicit layout hints.
Node cards expose engineering role badges derived from functional_role and separate QTY badges derived from normalized quantity.
QTY explicitly does not imply HA, peer membership or individual device decomposition.
Engineering connectivity filters provide All, Canonical, Physical, Logical, Management/OOB and Design views as presentation-only filters; canonical graph data is not mutated.
Canonical physical relationships render evidence-backed link metrics such as link quantity, speed and media when those attributes exist; parallel cables are not fabricated.
Design/presentation intents are labelled DESIGN and remain secondary/non-canonical.

Ring, HA/peer, EVPN and VXLAN badges appear only when explicit canonical relationship type/attributes contain supporting evidence; no topology protocol is inferred from quantity or visual arrangement.
Selected objects receive an Engineering Connectivity Evidence panel with canonical, physical and design-intent counts plus confirmed physical link attributes where available.
When endpoint port attributes are absent, the inspector explicitly states that port mapping is not present rather than inventing port names.
T03 Engineering view remains evidence-first and keeps design intents visually secondary.
Engineering hover magnification is reduced relative to the generic usability layer to avoid obscuring adjacent connectivity.

static_checks.method: balanced rule braces before repository write

static_checks.check: Files changed from pre-Iteration-4 baseline 80dc54c4d170205bf2e51a3d8199eb1ccad65020 through implementation head 10ca79d4fccee7bc94fbae1afb2107213f146b26

manual_acceptance_required: KAYAS T02 in ENGINEERING mode reads as a clear vertical engineering story: Security -> Edge/Interconnect -> Spine/Fabric Core -> Leaf/Access -> Management/OOB where objects exist.
SPINE, LEAF, FIREWALL, ADC, INTERCONNECT, OOB and other role badges match normalized functional_role values and do not introduce unsupported topology semantics.
QTY badges are visible without being interpreted as HA pairs.
Connectivity filters hide/show only presentation layers and never alter canonical counts.
KAYAS design paths remain clearly labelled DESIGN / non-confirmed.
KAYAS T03 still states that confirmed physical connectivity is not evidenced and does not fabricate ports, optics, speeds or A/B paths.
KAYAS T05 Management/OOB relationships remain visually distinguishable.
Selecting a KAYAS T02/T03/T05 object shows the Engineering Connectivity Evidence panel and does not invent physical link details.
No RING, HA/PEER, EVPN or VXLAN badge appears unless canonical evidence supports it.
Haven NORMALIZED_HINTS views retain their authored geometry.
Haven confirmed physical relationships show 4 x 100G, 16 x 25G SFP28 DAC and 12 x 25G SFP28 DAC metrics where those canonical attributes apply.
Haven physical inspector entries explicitly state missing endpoint port mapping when port attributes are absent.
Node hover does not materially obscure adjacent nodes or connections in Engineering mode.
Print remains usable and engineering controls do not appear as interactive clutter.
KAYAS and Haven production viewers remain unchanged.
notes: Iteration 4 implements the network-engineering review direction without changing the underlying DCTS canonical graph. The renderer is now more connection-centric in Engineering mode, but this checkpoint is not a browser/runtime PASS. Explicit user acceptance remains mandatory before any production promotion.
